Anchor-probe evidence (portfolio-core state/products/veridyn-ocr.json live_probe.drift_warnings + quality_gate.latest, Minor, both consistent): https://veridyn-ocr-dialect-service.vercel.app/api/health returns healthy but does not expose a running commit SHA, so source/runtime alignment for this product cannot be machine-verified from the outside — every other product in the roster with a public URL exposes this. Given F-31 (see the sibling security fingerprint on this board), OCR is exactly the shared-blast-radius service where identity verification matters most.

Done when: /api/health (or /api/version) returns a field carrying the deployed git commit SHA, and the anchor-probe drift warning for "runtime sha unknown" clears.

#23 Veridyn OCR: one shared static API key across six consumers, no per-consumer revocation

SAAD-17 finding F-31 (2026-07-10, re-verify against current source before fixing): Veridyn OCR is a shared service with six production consumers, all authenticating through one shared static API key. Consequences: rotating the key breaks all six consumers simultaneously (no staged rollover), there is no per-consumer revocation (a compromised or offboarded consumer cannot be cut off individually), no per-consumer rate limiting, no per-consumer attribution in logs, and (per the same finding) a single cached OCR worker that can die and stay dead with no restart signal.

OCR feeds the compliance/money-adjacent product surface (F-32 notes the intended OCR to Compliance integration), so a credential or availability incident here has portfolio-wide blast radius.

Done when: each of the six consumers authenticates with its own scoped, individually revocable credential, revoking one consumer's key is proven not to affect the others (live test), and per-consumer request attribution appears in logs.
